question.text: Vatsalya Charitable Society's AIR is being certified by Mr. Arjun Desai. The SE has not disclosed that one board member is also the founder-CEO of a vendor supplying 40% of its services. What reporting action is REQUIRED?

answer.text: Disclose the related-party relationship in the SIR as a limitation / assumption relevant to programme cost and impact attribution
Ignore — related-party information belongs in financial statements only

explanation.text: The Logic: Material related-party relationships can distort cost-per-beneficiary, cost-per-outcome, and attribution computations. Per Chapter 7.3.2 'assumptions and limitations', the SIA must disclose the RPT in the SIR so readers can assess impact credibly. The Trap: A artificially silos audit vs impact disclosures. C is unethical. D is nonsensical. Cross-Exam Context: RPT disclosure is tested in III-A/III-C Compliance (LODR Reg 23) and IND-AS 24. XXIII adds the impact-layer disclosure. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Build an RPT register into your engagement checklist. Reconcile the register against the SE's financial-statement RPT disclosures — any mismatch is a red flag worth a board-level conversation before signing off on the AIR.
